common_name: Legend of the Fall Fothergilla (Long-Holding Multi-Color Fall Foliage Hybrid)
scientific_name: Fothergilla x intermedia 'ALICE' (Legend of the Fall)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Legend of the Fall is an upright Proven Winners fothergilla hybrid bred for strong white bottlebrush blooms and an especially long-lasting red-orange-yellow fall color display.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade to full sun, and mulch to keep roots cool and evenly moist through summer heat. Legend of the Fall is an upright fothergilla hybrid bred for a heavy show of fragrant, honey-scented, bottlebrush-like white flower spikes in spring before the leaves emerge, followed by blue-green summer foliage that turns a spectacular, long-holding blend of red, orange, and yellow in fall — the display persists notably longer than in many older fothergilla selections. Its upright, four to five foot habit suits a shrub border, woodland edge, or foundation planting. Requires minimal pruning; simply remove dead or crossing wood after flowering if shaping is needed.
sources: Proven Winners ColorChoice — US Plant Patent USPP 32,049

common_name: Shoal Creek Chaste Tree (Classic Large-Spike Gulf South Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Shoal Creek, introduced in 1983 by Goodness Grows Nursery in Georgia, is the classic vitex selection for the Gulf South, valued for larger violet-blue flower spikes and faster, more vigorous growth than the straight species.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container specimens in well-drained, average to poor soil in full sun; Shoal Creek is the standard Gulf South chaste tree selection, chosen for noticeably longer, more densely flowered lavender-blue spikes and faster, more vigorous growth than seed-grown plants of the species. It blooms profusely on new growth from summer through fall, tolerating the heat, drought, and poor soil that defeat many other flowering shrubs, and the fragrant, gray-green palmately compound foliage adds a pleasant sage-like scent to the garden. Cutting back hard in late winter to 12-18 inches above ground produces vigorous new growth and the best flower display. It is a favorite of bees and butterflies through its long bloom season.

common_name: Blue Puffball Chaste Tree (True Dwarf Leaf Spot-Resistant Vitex)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Puffball is a true dwarf chaste tree, staying only about 3 by 4 feet, bred with leaf spot resistance and well suited to a small Gulf Coast garden or large container where a full-sized vitex would be too large.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Puffball is a genuine dwarf chaste tree, staying about 3 feet tall and 4 feet wide, a fraction of the size of the straight species, and bred with resistance to leaf spot that keeps its fragrant, gray-green foliage looking clean through a humid Gulf South summer. It produces the same lavender-blue flower spikes as full-sized vitex selections on a compact, rounded form suited to small beds, foundation plantings, or large containers. It blooms on new growth through summer into fall and tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil well once established. Cutting back lightly in late winter encourages fresh growth and continued heavy flowering.
sources: First Editions — US Plant Patent PP26775

common_name: Blue Diddley Chaste Tree (Compact Lavender-Blue Dwarf Vitex)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Diddley is a Proven Winners compact chaste tree, staying 3-6 feet tall, giving a smaller-scale alternative to full-sized vitex for a Gulf Coast bed or border.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Diddley is a compact chaste tree selection, staying 3-6 feet tall, considerably smaller than the classic 10-20 foot vitex species, making it easier to fit into a residential foundation planting or mixed border. It produces the same fragrant, gray-green foliage and lavender-blue flower spikes as larger vitex selections, blooming from summer into fall and tolerating heat, drought, and poor soil well once established. Its smaller stature means it needs less aggressive pruning than full-sized vitex; simply cut back lightly in late winter to encourage fresh growth and maintain a tidy shape.
